subject: Drafting Procurement Clause: No-Training Guarantee & TTL for Session Artifacts
messages:
From: Ayla Patterson <ayla@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement language: confirmation on non-training + TTL for logs

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this — our procurement team has asked for explicit warranty language around training and a clear TTL for operational artifacts (logs, traces, embeddings). Two quick asks we need answered before the SOW:

1) Can Redwood commit to a contractual clause that says "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, tune, or improve model weights or underlying model parameters"? We need the exact wording you would accept in the contract.

2) We also need a precise retention/TTL table for the artifacts that might contain customer content: request logs, debug traces, embeddings, temporary cache snapshots, backups. Our security team wants to map these to their data classification.

If you could provide a short statement and a technical appendix (or point us to a document) we can attach to the SOW, that would be ideal. If you have SOC2 evidence or a technical appendix that clarifies backups and snapshot behavior, please attach.

Best,
Ayla Patterson
Senior Counsel — Acme Health

Subject: Re: Procurement language: confirmation on non-training + TTL for logs

Ayla — thanks for the clear asks. Below is language we can commit to and a short TTL summary. I attached a technical appendix and our latest SOC 2 Type II report for your security team.

Contract language (suggested):
"Redwood does not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve the weights or parameters of any model. Customer Data will not be included in any datasets used to train, validate, or benchmark model weights, unless Redwood and Customer expressly agree in writing and the Customer provides affirmative opt-in for that use."

Operational caveats (non-training but practical):
- Operational/debugging data: short-lived request traces and error logs may be processed by Redwood engineers for debugging and incident response. Such artifacts are accessible only to authorized Redwood personnel and are purged according to the TTLs below unless retained for an active investigation.
- Aggregated telemetry: non-identifiable, aggregated metrics used for product health and capacity planning (e.g., p95 latency, token counts, error rates) are retained in aggregate form and do not include Customer Data in a way that could be reconstructed into original customer content.
- Embeddings: embeddings generated by the service are treated as derived customer artifacts. By default, embeddings are stored for up to 14 days to support affinity caching and replay protections; they are not used for model training. Customers can request/contract a shorter TTL or immediate deletion after delivery.
- Cache/snapshots: internal KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and cleared on a rolling basis; persistent snapshots that include user content are not used for training and are deleted per the backup retention schedule below.
- Backups & snapshots: backups of persistent storage that may contain customer content are retained for up to 90 days by default for disaster recovery. We can shorten this retention window in contract for regulated customers or commit to deletion-on-demand subject to typical technical constraints (e.g., restore windows).

TTL summary (default):
- Active request logs (request/response bodies): 30 days (technical debugging view restricted and redacted where feasible).
- Debug traces and extended logs: 90 days (used for troubleshooting, access restricted to SRE/engineers with justification).
- Embeddings (derived vectors): 14 days (configurable per contract).
- Aggregated telemetry/metrics: 365 days (no raw Customer Data).
- Backups/persistent snapshots: 90 days (option to shorten for contract).

Assurance notes:
- We maintain an internal tag/flagging system that marks customer content as "non-training" to ensure engineering experiments, model fine-tuning runs, and offline data pipelines exclude these records.
- Any request to include customer data in research/training requires a documented opt-in workflow involving Legal and Customer approval.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2028.pdf; Non-Training_Guarantee_Technical_Appendix.pdf (includes flow diagrams and exact deletion APIs).

If this looks good, Marissa can shepherd the language into the SOW and we can provide an exhibit with the appendix. Happy to make the TTLs shorter if Acme requires it for compliance.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — this is helpful. Two follow-ups from our InfoSec team:

1) Backups: when you say backups are retained for up to 90 days by default, is that a single retention for all backup tiers? Do you have immutable backups or point-in-time snapshots that could persist beyond deletion requests? We need to map whether customer deletion requests will be reflected in backups and how long until purged.

2) Cache snapshots: our engineering team asked whether cache population (e.g., prefix caching of prompt prefixes, KV entries) could persist longer than the stated TTL in edge cases (restarts, warmable caches). Is there an API to purge these caches immediately?

Can you confirm these two points in writing so we can include them as exceptions/clarifications in the SOW?

Best,
Ayla

Ayla — quick answers on behalf of infra:

1) Backups & deletion:
- Our backups use a layered retention policy. Logical deletion requests are applied to our primary store and flagged for purge. Immutable backups (for compliance/forensics) are retained only for the disaster recovery window and are included in the 90-day retention by default. If you require a shorter window or deletion-of-backups-on-request, we can include that as a negotiated term; note that some disaster-recovery guarantees may be impacted.

2) Cache snapshots & purge API:
- Cache behavior: prefix/KV caches are designed to be ephemeral and are not intended as durable storage. We have an internal purge endpoint that operators can call to flush caches for a specific customer keyspace. We will expose a contract-backed API "/v1/admin/purge-customer-cache" as an option in the SOW for regulated customers; calls to the API will be logged and the purge completes within minutes in normal operation.

If helpful, Marissa can include the exact admin API path in the exhibit and we can add the optional shorter backup retention term as a negotiable checkbox in the SOW.

-Sean
